spots.name: Osaka Castle
spots.summary: Osaka Castle is a Japanese castle in Chūō-ku, Osaka, Japan. The castle is one of Japan's most famous landmarks and played a major role in the unification of Japan during the sixteenth century of the Azuchi–Momoyama period.

spots.name: Abeno Harukas
spots.summary: Abeno Harukas (あべのハルカス) is a multi-purpose commercial facility in Abenosuji Itchome, Abeno-ku, Osaka, Japan. It consists of the New Annex, Eastern Annex and a supertall skyscraper, Abeno Harukas.

spots.name: Universal Studios Japan
spots.summary: Universal Studios Japan (ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン) is a theme park located in Osaka, Japan. Opened on March 31, 2001, it is one of six Universal Studios theme parks worldwide and was the first to open outside the United States. The park is owned and operated by USJ LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Comcast NBCUniversal.

names.ja: ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン

spots.name: Shitennō-ji

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Shitennō-ji is a Buddhist temple in Ōsaka, Japan. It is also known as Arahaka-ji (荒陵寺), Nanba-ji/Naniwa-daiji (難波大寺), or Mitsu-ji 御津寺.

spots.name: Umeda Sky Building

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Umeda Sky Building is a two-tower mixed-use skyscraper in Osaka, Japan.

spots.name: Tsūtenkaku
spots.summary: Tsūtenkaku is a tower and landmark of Osaka, Japan, and advertises the Hitachi company. It is located in the Shinsekai district of Naniwa-ku, Osaka. Its total height is 108 metres (354 ft); the main observation deck is at a height of 91 metres (299 ft). It is owned by Tsūtenkaku Kanko Co., Ltd. .

spots.name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
spots.summary: The Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan is an aquarium located in the ward of Minato in Osaka, Osaka Prefecture, Japan, near Osaka Bay. When it opened in 1990, it was the largest public aquarium in the world.

spots.name: Ishiyama Hongan-ji

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ishiyama Hongan-ji (石山本願寺) was the primary fortress of the Ikkō-ikki, leagues of warrior priests and commoners who opposed samurai rule during the Sengoku period. It was established in 1496, at the mouth of the Yodo River, on the coast of the Seto Inland Sea.

spots.name: Mount Tenpō
spots.summary: Mount Tenpō , located in Minato-ku, Osaka, is Japan's second lowest mountain. The mountain's peak is 4.53 metres (14.9 ft) above sea level, and bears more resemblance to a hill than a mountain. A small port is located nearby, and much of the mountain's surface has been converted into a park.

spots.name: Naniwa-kyō
spots.summary: Naniwa-kyō (難波京) was a historical Japanese capital city, located in present-day central Osaka city.

spots.name: Grand Green Osaka
spots.summary: Grand Green Osaka (グラングリーン大阪) /Umekita Park is a 24-hectare (59-acre) civic project being developed in Osaka. Most of the park opened on September 6, 2024.

spots.name: Osaka Castle Park
spots.summary: Osaka Castle Park is a public urban park and historical site situated at Osaka-Jō in Chūō-ku, Osaka, Japan. It lies on the south of the Ōkawa and occupies a large area in the center of the city of Osaka. This park is the second largest park in the city.

spots.name: Gate Tower Building

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Gate Tower Building is a 16-floor office building in Fukushima-ku, Osaka, Japan. It is notable for the highway offramp of the Ikeda Route that passes through the building.

spots.name: Osaka Tenmangū
spots.summary: The Osaka Tenmangū Shrine is a Shinto shrine and one of Tenmangū founded in AD 949 in Osaka by Emperor Murakami. The Tenjin Festival is held here annually from 24 July to 25 July. The shrine has been periodically destroyed by fire, with the present entrance hall and gate built in 1845.

spots.name: Nakanoshima Museum of Art, Osaka

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Nakanoshima Museum of Art, Osaka opened in Nakanoshima, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan in 2022. The museum is located in the central Nakanoshima district of Osaka.

spots.name: Hollywood Dream – The Ride
spots.summary: Hollywood Dream – The Ride is a steel roller coaster located at Universal Studios Japan. Designed by Bolliger & Mabillard, it features inbuilt sound systems allowing riders to choose their ride music.

spots.name: Tennōji Zoo

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Tennōji Zoo (天王寺動物園) is a 11-hectare (27-acre) zoo located at Tennōji Park in Tennōji-ku, Osaka, Japan, opened on January 1, 1915. It is the third zoo to be built in Japan and is located southwest of the Shitennō-ji temple, the first Buddhist temple in Japan.

spots.name: Festivalgate
spots.summary: Festivalgate was an amusement park in the Shinsekai district of Naniwa, Osaka, Japan, just beside the Shin-Imamiya Station of the Osaka Loop Line of Nishinihon Japan Railway and Nankai Railway.

names.ja: フェスティバルゲート

spots.name: Glico Man
spots.summary: The Glico Man , also referred to as the Glico Running Man, is a giant neon sign and billboard located next to the Dōtonbori canal in Dōtonbori district, Osaka, Japan. It depicts a runner with both arms raised as he crosses a finish line on a blue running track.

spots.name: Tekijuku
spots.summary: Tekijuku was a private school of Dutch studies (Rangaku) in Osaka, Japan. Ogata Kōan, a doctor and scholar of Rangaku, established it in 1838 during the Tenpō era of the late Edo period. Its official name was Tekitekisaijuku (適々斎塾), named after one of Ogata's art names, Tekitekisai (適々斎).

spots.name: Osaka City Central Public Hall
spots.summary: Osaka City Central Public Hall is a public building in the city of Osaka, situated on the Nakanoshima sandbank.

spots.name: Nipponbashi
spots.summary: Nipponbashi is a shopping district of Naniwa Ward, Osaka, Japan. The area is centered along Sakaisuji Avenue, extending from the Ebisu-chō Interchange of the Hanshin Expressway in the south, to Nansan-dōri in the north.

spots.name: Tennōji Park
spots.summary: The Tennōji Park is a park with botanical garden at 1–108, Chausuyama-cho, Tennōji-ku, Osaka, Japan.

spots.name: Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts (大阪市立美術館) is a museum located in Tennōji Park, Tennōji-ku, Osaka, Japan. The museum focuses on Japanese and east Asian art.

spots.name: Mario Kart: Bowser's Challenge
spots.summary: Mario Kart: Bowser's Challenge is an augmented reality dark ride that serves as the anchor attraction of Super Nintendo World at Universal Studios Japan, Universal Studios Hollywood, and Universal Epic Universe.

spots.name: Imamiya Ebisu Shrine

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Imamiya Ebisu Shrine is a Shinto shrine located in Naniwa-ku, Osaka Prefecture, Japan. According to legend, it was established in 600 during the reign of Empress Suiko. Its annual festival is held from January 9 to 11.

spots.name: Abenobashi Terminal Building
spots.summary: Abeno Harukas (あべのハルカス) is a multi-purpose commercial facility in Abenosuji Itchome, Abeno-ku, Osaka, Japan. It consists of the New Annex, Eastern Annex and a supertall skyscraper, Abeno Harukas.

names.ja: 阿部野橋ターミナルビル

spots.name: Ikasuri Shrine

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ikasuri Shrine is a major Shinto shrine located in central Osaka, Japan. Its annual festival is on April 22. In the former modern system of ranked Shinto shrines it was an imperial shrine of the second rank or kanpei-chūsha (官幣中社). It was also the ichinomiya of the former Settsu Province.

spots.name: Osaka Museum of History

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: Osaka Museum of History opened in Chūō-ku, Ōsaka, Japan, in 2001. The project architects were César Pelli & Associates and Nihon Sekkei. It is adjoined by an atrium to the NHK Osaka Broadcasting Center, which was designed by the same architects and built at the same time.

spots.name: Ikukunitama Shrine

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ikukunitama Shrine is a Shinto shrine located in Tennōji-ku, Osaka Prefecture, Japan. Its main festival is held annually on September 9. It was formerly an imperial shrine of the first rank in the Modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines.

spots.name: Hōkoku Shrine

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hōkoku Shrine is a Shinto shrine located in Osaka, Japan. It is one of several Toyokuni shrines built in honor of Toyotomi Hideyoshi. It is part of the Osaka Castle Park.

spots.name: Isshin-ji

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Isshin-ji (一心寺) is a Pure Land Buddhist temple in Osaka, Japan. Starting in the Meiji period, thirteen images have been formed, each incorporating the ashes of tens of thousands of devotees. The annual burial ceremony on 21 April in turn draws tens of thousands of worshippers.

spots.name: Hōzen-ji

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Hōzen-ji (法善寺) is a Buddhist temple of the Jōdo-shū sect in Chūō-ku, Osaka, Japan. The temple is located in the Dotonbori district, near Namba Station. It has a reputation in Japan for helping women who are about to give birth.

spots.name: Namba Parks
spots.summary: Namba Parks is an office and shopping complex located in Namba-naka Nichome, Naniwa-ku, Osaka, Japan, the south of Namba Station on Nankai Railway. It consists of a high-rise office building called Parks Tower and a 120-tenant shopping mall with rooftop garden.

spots.name: The Flying Dinosaur
spots.summary: The Flying Dinosaur is a steel flying roller coaster at Universal Studios Japan. Designed by Swiss firm Bolliger & Mabillard, Flying Dinosaur restrains riders in the prone position.

spots.name: Taiyū-ji

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Taiyū-ji (太融寺) is a Buddhist temple in Osaka Prefecture, Japan. It was founded in 821.

spots.name: Osaka Business Park
spots.summary: Osaka Business Park is a business district of Chūō-ku, Osaka, Japan. The area spans 26 hectares northeast of Osaka Castle Park, and is bordered by the Neyagawa and Daini-Neyagawa rivers.

spots.name: National Museum of Art, Osaka

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri

spots.summary: The National Museum of Art, Osaka is a subterranean Japanese art museum located on the island of Nakanoshima, located between the Dōjima River and the Tosabori River, about 10 minutes west of Higobashi Station in central Osaka.

spots.name: HEP
spots.summary: HEP is a major shopping mall and entertainment center in the Umeda commercial district of Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan. It is a shopping mall consisting of a HEP Five and HEP Navio.

spots.name: Osaka City Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Osaka City Museum is a former museum dedicated to the history of Ōsaka, Japan. Located in the former headquarters of the 4th Division of the Imperial Japanese Army in Osaka Castle Park, the ground floor opened to the public in December 1960, with the special exhibition Momoyama Culture.

spots.name: Sakuya Konohana Kan
spots.summary: The Sakuya Konohana Kan (咲くやこの花館) is a botanical garden set within one of the world's largest greenhouses, located in Tsurumi Ryokuchi park at 2-163 Ryokuchi Koen, Tsurumi-ku, Osaka, Japan. It is open daily except Mondays; an admission fee is charged.

spots.name: Umeda Arts Theater
spots.summary: Umeda Arts Theater is a Japanese theater located at Chayamachi Applause in Chayamachi, Kita-ku, Osaka, operated by Umeda Arts Theater Co., Ltd. It opened in 1992.

spots.name: Museum of Oriental Ceramics, Osaka

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of Oriental Ceramics, Osaka (大阪市立東洋陶磁美術館) is a Japanese art museum and regarded as one of the best ceramic-collections in the world. This museum collects, studies, conserves, exhibits and interprets East Asian ceramics, which mainly came from ancient China and Korea.

spots.name: Modern Transportation Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Modern Transportation Museum was the corporate museum operated by West Japan Railway Company in Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan. It opened on 21 January 1962, next to Bentencho Station on the Osaka Loop Line.

spots.name: Space Fantasy – The Ride
spots.summary: Space Fantasy – The Ride is a spinning roller coaster at Universal Studios Japan in Osaka, Japan. The ride opened on March 18, 2010, as a replacement for the E.T. Adventure dark ride.

spots.name: Fujita Art Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Fujita Art Museum is one of the largest private collections in the Kansai region. The collection was assembled by Fujita Denzaburō and his descendants. It was installed in a storehouse on the family property in Osaka.

If there's a queue at the original outlet (and there usually is), there are t

spots.name: Ajinoya
spots.summary: Some of the best okonomiyaki in Osaka, and they're so proud of it they prepare it for you from start to end, making a good choice for the casual visitor as well. The "A set" (¥5,900) includes no less than four styles and will leave four people stuffed to the gills. Very popular, so join the queue early, and beware that ordering here is once and done: you can't add on more later.

spots.name: Taiyoshi Hyakuban
spots.summary: Most of the "restaurants" in the area are really brothels in disguise (since prostitution is illegal in Japan), but this extravagant century-old brothel is a Tangible Cultural Property that has been turned into an actual restaurant open to the public. Specialities include hot pot dishes like sukiyaki and yosenabe.

spots.summary: Jan-Jan Yokocho is a famous shopping street along a narrow lane. There are still many establishments running in the same shops they built immediately after World War II. The entire area is squashed with small, cheap eating houses.
